intro: EHN Willowview Recovery Centre is a residential addiction treatment centre near Lumsden, about 30 km northwest of Regina. EHN Canada runs it for the Saskatchewan Health Authority, which pays for the program, so eligible Saskatchewan adults are treated at no cost.

With room for up to 60 clients, it is the largest addictions treatment facility in the province. The base program is 8 weeks and can stretch to 16, with nurses on site around the clock and a team of counsellors, medical staff and addiction support workers.

pillars.title: Eight Weeks of Care, With Room to Stay Longer
pillars.body: Treatment starts with an 8 week residential program, and clients who need more time can extend to a total of 16 weeks. EHN lists detox as part of care, and nurses are on site 24/7. The days are built around group and one-on-one therapy using CBT, DBT and relapse prevention, with psychoeducation, meditation and breathwork. EHN says family dynamics are part of how counsellors plan care, and the program includes Indigenous cultural healing practices.

pillars.title: A Renovated Retreat in the Qu'Appelle Valley
pillars.body: Willowview is on Grid Road 724 outside Lumsden, a small town in the Qu'Appelle Valley about half an hour from Regina. The centre took over the former Living Skies Retreat, which was renovated before the province opened all 60 inpatient spaces in 2025. EHN's photos show a brick main building with a tall spire and open lawns running out to the valley hills. Clients have access to a gym and outdoor activities on site.

pillars.title: Staying Connected Through EHN Alumni
pillars.body: When the residential stay ends, clients can join the EHN Canada Alumni Association. Members get outreach calls, emails and invitations to special events and recovery celebrations. Saskatchewan residents can also look at the province's funded virtual programs that EHN runs, which are listed on the EHN website alongside Willowview.

overviewH2: EHN Willowview Recovery Centre: Centre Overview
overview: Willowview came out of Saskatchewan's plan to add 500 addiction treatment spaces. The Saskatchewan Health Authority chose EHN Canada through a request for proposals, and the opening ran late: the centre was first expected in spring 2024 and offered day treatment while fire safety renovations were finished. The first 20 inpatient beds opened in January 2025 and the remaining 40 began intake on April 1, 2025.

faqIntro: Answers come from the EHN Canada website, the Government of Saskatchewan and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is EHN Willowview Recovery Centre free?
faqs.a: Yes, for Saskatchewan residents. EHN says all programs at Willowview are fully funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, so eligible residents pay nothing for treatment. People from outside the province are not accepted at this time.
Adults 18 and older who live in Saskatchewan and have a valid Saskatchewan health card. The program is for people whose main concern is a substance use disorder.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Willowview?
faqs.a: The core residential program is 8 weeks. Clients can extend their stay, up to a total of 16 weeks in care, and the province describes the centre as offering up to 16 weeks of treatment.
EHN lists detox as one part of treatment at Willowview, and nurses are on site 24 hours a day. Ask the admissions team how withdrawal would be handled in your situation before you arrive.

faqs.q: How do I get into Willowview?
faqs.a: Start with the inquiry form on the EHN Willowview web page; the admissions team reviews each form and follows up. You can also call EHN Canada admissions at 1-866-963-6343.

faqs.q: How many people does Willowview treat at once?
faqs.a: Up to 60 clients at a time. The province opened all 60 inpatient spaces in 2025 and calls Willowview the largest addictions treatment facility in Saskatchewan.

faqs.q: What therapies are used at Willowview?
faqs.a: Treatment centres on cognitive behavioural therapy, dialectical behaviour therapy and relapse prevention, delivered in group and one-on-one sessions with psychoeducation. EHN also lists meditation, breathwork, Indigenous cultural healing practices and family and cultural support.

faqs.q: Where is Willowview and how far is it from Regina?
faqs.a: The centre is at 724 Grid Road near Lumsden, in the Qu'Appelle Valley about 30 km northwest of Regina. That is roughly a 30 minute drive from Regina, about an hour from Moose Jaw and around two and a half hours from Saskatoon.

faqs.q: What support is there after Willowview?
faqs.a: Graduates can join the EHN Canada Alumni Association. Members get outreach calls, emails and invitations to special events and recovery celebrations.

EHN Canada, a private treatment network that also runs centres in Ontario and British Columbia. The Saskatchewan Health Authority picked EHN through a request for proposals and funds the beds under a service agreement.
